speaker: Doctor
text: I notice you mentioned the infant has increasing yellow discoloration of the eyes and skin. How many hours old is the baby, and was this jaundice present at birth or did it develop after a few days?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-week-old female newborn. The patient has been experiencing increasing yellow discoloration of her eyes and skin for 2 days. She was born at 39 weeks' gestation, initially weighed 3066 g and now weighs 3200 g. The patient is exclusively breastfed.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Breastfeeding Jaundice (Suboptimal Intake Jaundice). The infant is a 2-week-old with worsening jaundice, exclusively breastfed, and stable weight gain; this clinical picture is classic for inadequate caloric intake rather than pathological hyperbilirubinemia. I recommend checking a total serum bilirubin level to confirm and rule out hemolysis, and ensuring the mother provides more frequent feeding sessions to increase stooling.
